item.title: Aspens 'remember' past drought in their leaves, 3-year experiment finds
item.description: Drought is written into trees, appearing as narrow bands in their annual growth rings. item.title: Un fuerte terremoto de magnitud 7,7 sacude Panamá
item.description: Un terremoto de magnitud 7,6 ha sacudido Panamá este viernes, según el Servicio Geológico de Estados Unidos (USGS), y ha desatado el pánico en la capital de los rascacielos. El seísmo ha activado también la alerta de tsunami, que ha sido posteriormente retirada.El USGS ha informado inicialmente de una magnitud de 8, pero la ha rebajado poco después a 7,6, y ha ubicado su epicentro a 10 kilómetros de Pitaloza Arriba, en el centro sur del país. Poco después se han producido réplicas de 6,1, 6,0 y la más reciente de 5,3.Aunque inicialmente no se reportaron daños estructurales de relevancia, sí… Publicado también por: ABC España - Internacional, Noticias Telemundo. Fuente: BBC News Mundo.

item.title: Ranch Relisted After Wildfire: Turkey Track returns at $180 million; restored Texas Panhandle giant
item.description: Turkey Track Ranch, a storied expanse in the Texas Panhandle, is back on the market with a price tag of $180 million after extensive revitalization. item.title: Climate change drives new species combinations, prompting calls to rethink conservation goals
item.description: The fact that ecosystems change is nothing new. What is new, however, is the speed and scale at which new species communities are emerging as a result of climate change. item.description: Storm expected to make landfall on US’s northern Gulf coast with risk of flash floods and isolated river flooding Isaias has become the first Atlantic hurricane of the 2026 season, with wind speeds of 80mph and a minimum pressure of 975mb. It is expected to strengthen to a category 2 hurricane as it approaches the US’s northern Gulf coast on Friday, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). As a result of the strong El Niño , it has been a notably quiet Atlantic hurricane season. The first hurricane of the season has not formed this late since 8 October 1905… Publicado también por: The Guardian - Environment. Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: Almost 300,000 people now live in flood‑prone areas in the Nepalese Himalayas—new research
item.description: On Aug. 26, a rock and ice avalanche triggered a huge flood that swept through a steep valley in Nepal, leaving thousands dead and missing. It was an extreme example of a growing problem across the Himalayas. As glaciers melt, glacial lakes expand and mountain permafrost thaws, the risks from floods, landslides and other high-mountain hazards are increasing. At the same time, more people and infrastructure are moving into the valleys where these hazards are most likely to strike. Fuente: Phys.org.
